text.p: These are the highlights of main stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Although the European Union allowed Macedonia to sign a textile deal early, it cannot be implemented for the time being because competent bodies failed to issue certificates for export licences.
- Macedonia will by end August sign bilateral agreement with three Paris Club countries (USA, Japan and Italy) on rescheduling its $315 million debt. Macedonia's total debt stands at $1.1 billion.

- Prilep District Attorney launched criminal proceedings against 7 individuals for insulting the dignity of the Republic of Macedonia during the celebration of the Ilinden national holiday in Krusevo, when they trampled on the Macedonian flag.
- The opposition VRMO-DPMNE party protested against police interrogation of its members, which the Constitutional Court proclaimed illegal last year.
- U.S. Ambassador to Skopje Christopher Hill presented Macedonia with $1.7 million worth of road construction equipment on Thursday.

- In accordance with World Bank and IMF suggestions, the Macedonian Parliament will debate amendments to the labour law in September, envisaging cutting maternity leave from 9 to 6 months and the annual vacation from 18 to 12 days. -- Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
